text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSLITA

- Poland's Foreign Trade Minister Jacek Buchacz was sacked because of public funds' ill-management and planned transfer of hundreds of millions of dollars to a private bank in Ukraine, Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said in a TV address on Saturday.
- US Findlay Industries, which supplies car upholstery to General Motors (GM), will invest 13 million zlotys in a new plant in Tomaszow Mazowiecki, central Poland.
- Hochland Poland cheesemaker will soon double its production capacity to meet the demand in Poland and other countries in the region, Hochland Poland marketing director Miroslaw Stec said.

- The British RMC construction material firm has given up plans to purchase a stake in Nowa Huta cement mill after the talks on forming a joint venture with plant's strategic investors, the Turkish Rumeli group, came to no avail.

- Increased industrial output and sales this year brought no higher profits to Polish firms as their financial results proved worse in 1996's first half, compared with the same period last year, the planning ministry's report said.
- Belgian Diamond Suppliers (BDS) will open a Diamond Trading Centre in Poznan three to four years after Poland introduces wholesale diamond sale regulations, BDS representatives said.
- Renault Poland has lost around 4.5 million zlotys due to the recently introduced regulations on limiting car imports, Renault preliminary estimates said.
NOWA EUROPA
- Poland will receive a $67 million loan from World Bank to help finance a $145 million programme to modernise access to sea ports.
- Poland's imports from CEFTA countries reached more than $735 million in 1995 and were 20 percent higher than exports, which exceeded $570 million, Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- The Anglo-Dutch Gaspol firm will invest $40 million in the the Gdansk port-based liquid gas terminal construction. The terminal reloading capacity will reach 500 million cubic metres.
- Poland's president Alexander Kwasniewski has met with British Petroleum representatives to discuss the concern's investment plans in this country.
- International E-4 road in Nowy Sacz province, southern Poland, was flooded following the two day heavy rainfalls last weekend.
- Warsaw bourse WIG main market index will reach 16,832 points by December-end, Nowa Europa's monthly survey of brokerage houses showed.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- International firms have declared over $1 billion investments in the newly created Special Economic Zone in the industrial Katowice province, southern Poland.
- Poland's leading Szczecin Shipyard wants to form a holding firm covering Czestochowa steel mill, Poznan Cegielski ship engine maker and Gdynia shipyard.

- Nissan Poland and TBWA advertising agency will start a multimedial advertising campaign of the Nissan Primera passenger car model. In the next two years the campaign will cost $3 million, TBWA president Waldemar Duszynski said.

- Dutch RTL7 television plans to lounch a satellite Polish language programme transmitted from Luxembourg this year and is now in talks on cooperation with the Polish cable TV networks Porion, PTK, and Aster City, RTL7 representatives said.
ZYCIE WARSZAWY
- Daewoo has ordered 100 Sokol helicopters worth $100 million from the PZL Swidnik helicopter maker.
- According to a survey by the CBOS polling institute, 42 percent of Poles think privatisation is too slow, while 19 percent find it too quick. Sixteen percent think it is satisfactory.
